tasks.short: Monitor complaint handling, resolve procedural delays, and revise complaint procedures.

steps.what: Gather case dates, procedural stages, and assigned owners from the restricted complaint register.
Compare case progress with deadlines and identify missing updates.
Request progress updates from case owners and arrange overdue reviews.
Discuss delays, procedural fairness, and necessary exceptions with case owners.
Draft procedural revisions and explain proposed changes.

loop.input: Current complaint procedure, agreed change requirements, and approved legal guidance.
loop.output: Procedure revision with a change summary and source references.
loop.check: Validate references and required sections; officer checks fairness, deadlines, and escalation rights.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved legal questions return to the officer and legal adviser.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but changes require contextual wording across several policy sections.

steps.what: Approve the revised procedure after legal advice and any required employee consultation.
Publish the approved procedure and notify affected case owners.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted case register, deadlines, reminders, and approvals in the {WORKFLOW}, importing existing complaint metadata through the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded drafting loop prepares revisions in the {DOCS}; people decide procedural exceptions and approve changes before publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case dates, ownership, and procedure versions were disconnected. Confidentiality and procedural exceptions made generic reminders difficult to introduce.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, access controls, and approval flows cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting metadata and generating revision drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Contested deadlines, retaliation concerns, investigator independence, and national rules need human interpretation. Access restrictions must survive every integration.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a delay reflects fear, conflict, or an unfair process, and secure a credible remedy.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on procedural bottlenecks before complaint deadlines are missed.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time collecting dates and chasing routine updates. The role can gain authority to convene urgent procedural reviews within an agreed escalation policy; complaint findings remain with authorised investigators.

reach.task: Review grievance escalation routes and employee representation arrangements.
reach.learn: How representation rights, collective arrangements, and national rules affect complaint handling.

evidence.claim: Restricted registers, deadline checks, reminders, and versioned approvals are feasible with configured workflows and deterministic integrations.
Complaint interpretation and procedural fairness require accountable human judgement.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Dutch works council consent requirements cover specified employee-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require national assessment.

assumptions: The baseline uses a restricted complaint register in the {SPREADSHEET}, with documents in the {DOCS}.
The {WORKFLOW} can provide suitable confidentiality, retention, and access controls.
Automated reminders contain minimal case metadata and use approved internal recipients.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
EU law applies; consultation and complaint procedure requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Current complaint channels, register location, and access permissions.
Actual complaint deadlines, escalation powers, and exception volumes.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
Whether existing workflow licensing supports restricted case records.
Who may approve procedure changes and deadline exceptions.
research_questions: Which existing workflow controls meet the required confidentiality and retention model?
Which reminders can use fixed wording without revealing complaint details?
Can procedure drafting work entirely from approved policies without case narratives?
new_work: Review reminder exceptions and incorrect ownership.
Maintain deadline rules and approved recipient groups.
Review procedure drafts and source references.
Check access logs, retention, and failed integrations.

tasks.short: Advise and train managers and employees on fair employment practices and grievance procedures.

steps.what: Read advice requests and identify the audience, urgency, and sensitive case context.
Find current policies, approved legal guidance, and relevant training examples.
Prepare audience-specific explanations, exercises, and session materials.

loop.input: Audience brief, approved guidance pack, and training template; no identifiable complaint narratives.
loop.output: Training materials with cited guidance and fictional exercises.
loop.check: Check source versions and links; officer reviews legal meaning, accessibility, and examples.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported guidance is omitted and referred to the officer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates cannot fully adapt explanations and exercises to different audiences.

steps.what: Deliver training and discuss how fair practices apply in everyday decisions.
Discuss sensitive situations privately and agree appropriate next steps.
Record attendance, distribute approved resources, and assign follow-up learning.

tasks.design: Configure topic-based retrieval of approved guidance in the {DOCS} and learning records in the {LMS}. A bounded loop drafts audience-specific materials for officer review before delivery, while the {WORKFLOW} distributes approved resources and records completion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance was scattered and session materials needed repeated adaptation. Sensitive advice could not safely be reduced to a generic answer.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned source libraries and reusable templates support reliable retrieval. Bounded drafting can reduce preparation effort without replacing live discussion.
tasks.still_hard: People may describe disputes indirectly or ask for reassurance about a contested decision. Legal interpretation, trust, accessibility, and national rules remain demanding.
tasks.human_edge: Help people recognise unfair behaviour, challenge assumptions, and discuss difficult situations without discouraging disclosure.

ambition.what: Short fair-supervision clinics for newly appointed frontline supervisors.

tasks.altitude: Preparation and attendance administration shrink, leaving more time for practice sessions and private advice. The officer can gain discretion over clinic topics and scheduling; authority over employment decisions does not change.

reach.task: Design scenario exercises and evaluate learning transfer.
reach.learn: Adult learning, accessible facilitation, and how to test changes in supervisory behaviour.

reach.task: Explain fair hiring procedures to hiring managers.
reach.learn: Where recruitment policy becomes concrete interview, selection, and documentation decisions.

evidence.claim: Approved document retrieval and learning administration can use configured software.
A bounded drafting loop can prepare training materials, with human checks of legal meaning and audience suitability.
The documented report failure involving invented sources supports checking generated references before use.

assumptions: Current policy documents and learning materials have identifiable owners and approval dates.
The company uses the {LMS} for attendance or completion records.
Retrieval returns approved source passages rather than making employment decisions.
Training drafts use fictional examples and exclude identifiable complaint details.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Advice demand, audience languages, and accessibility needs.
Quality and coverage of the approved guidance library.
Existing permissions and integration options in the {DOCS} and {LMS}.
Whether attendance recording changes require consultation under national rules.
Who approves training materials and handles legal escalations.
research_questions: Can existing document search meet routine retrieval needs without a model?
Which supervisor topics benefit most from short practice clinics?
What source coverage is needed before drafting materials for each topic?
new_work: Maintain guidance ownership, versions, and topic labels.
Review draft examples and remove unsupported statements.
Handle questions outside the approved guidance.
Maintain learning assignments and check failed completion updates.

tasks.short: Survey employees and assess whether employment practices show patterns consistent with systemic discrimination.

steps.what: Agree survey purpose, lawful data collection, confidentiality, and consultation requirements.
Select questions and tailor the survey using approved wording and response options.
Check the final questionnaire and release invitations to the approved survey population.
Monitor participation, send agreed reminders, and close response collection.
Clean responses and prepare permitted employment comparisons with disclosure controls.
Calculate group comparisons, response bias checks, and uncertainty measures.
Interpret statistics and comments, test alternative explanations, and decide further investigation needs.

tasks.design: Configure approved questionnaires, invitations, and response collection in the {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic jobs in the {DATA_PLATFORM} prepare permitted comparisons from the {HCM} and {ATS}, enforce disclosure controls, and feed the {BI}; the officer interprets findings and recommends investigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Survey exports and employment records needed manual alignment. Small groups, inconsistent definitions, and lawful collection requirements limited reusable analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: Survey configuration and reproducible statistical code already exist. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building validation, disclosure controls, and repeatable comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: Low participation, small samples, confounding, and fear of identification can distort findings. Statistical differences alone do not establish unlawful discrimination.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a credible systemic concern from an artefact of sampling or context, while protecting employees who disclose experiences.

ambition.what: Quarterly prioritisation of employment practices needing targeted investigation.

tasks.altitude: The officer spends less time cleaning responses and rebuilding comparisons, and more time testing explanations. A formal mandate could allow the officer to initiate a scoped fact-finding review; findings do not automatically trigger individual employment actions.

reach.role: compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialist
reach.task: Build comparable job groups for pay and progression analysis.
reach.learn: Job evaluation, defensible comparison groups, and the limits of adjusted pay comparisons.

reach.task: Prioritise investigation of recruitment and progression practices.
reach.learn: How evidence thresholds, management context, and remedy authority shape an investigation.

evidence.claim: Survey distribution, validation, statistical calculations, and disclosure controls can be configured or coded deterministically.
Special-category processing needs an applicable GDPR Article 9 condition as well as an Article 6 legal basis.
The cited Dutch DPIA list includes employee monitoring; national lists and the GDPR risk assessment must be checked elsewhere.
AI used for specified employment evaluation purposes can fall within the AI Act's employment high-risk category.

assumptions: Collection uses approved questions and does not infer protected characteristics from names, photographs, or text.
Protected-characteristic data are processed only where a lawful basis and any required special-category condition exist.
Individual survey linkage occurs only if expressly authorised in the survey plan; otherwise comparisons use suitable aggregates.
A survey described as anonymous has no retained identity linkage.
Small-cell suppression also considers indirect identification across repeated reports.
EU law applies; national rules govern additional consultation and employment requirements.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Applicable country, legal bases, and permitted demographic categories.
Whether the survey is anonymous, confidential, or lawfully linked to employment records.
Existing questionnaire, sampling method, and statistical expertise.
Actual group sizes, response coverage, and data quality.
Required consultation, impact assessments, retention, and access approvals.
research_questions: Which comparisons are supportable given participation, sample sizes, and lawful data availability?
Which disclosure controls protect small groups across successive survey waves?
Can aggregate comparisons answer the investigation question without individual linkage?
Does the proposed use require an AI Act assessment, even if the statistical pipeline uses no AI?
new_work: Review data quality exceptions and changes to comparison groups.
Maintain questionnaires, analysis specifications, and disclosure controls.
Check participation bias and uncertainty before interpretation.
Handle privacy questions and requests for follow-up investigation.
Reassess access, retention, and survey linkage when scope changes.

tasks.short: Report selection and survey statistics and recommend corrective action.

steps.what: Collect selection records, employment figures, survey statistics, and previous action updates.
Reconcile periods, denominators, categories, and missing records.
Calculate statistics and assemble charts with uncertainty and disclosure controls.
Draft the report narrative, methods, limitations, and action progress summary.

loop.input: Validated statistics, chart descriptions, methods, approved source notes, and recorded action status.
loop.output: Draft report narrative with traceable factual statements and explicit limitations.
loop.check: Validate every number against the dataset and every citation against the source pack; officer checks interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported statements are removed and unresolved sections use a factual template.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed templates handle tables, but changing findings and limitations need contextual prose.

steps.what: Assess corrective options with responsible managers and recommend proportionate action.
Approve the report, recipients, and corrective action commitments.
Publish the approved report internally and record action owners and deadlines.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs in the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile approved extracts from the {ATS}, {HCM}, and {PROJECT}, then generate statistics and charts for the {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts source-grounded narrative; people choose remedies and approve recipients before the {WORKFLOW} publishes the report and updates action records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated exports used inconsistent definitions, and charts were manually copied into documents. Recommendations required contextual evidence beyond the numbers.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data contracts, deterministic report generation, and bounded drafting can reduce assembly effort. AI-assisted coding can make the connecting code cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Selection data may omit relevant context or lawful demographic information. Corrective actions need credible causal reasoning, authority, resources, and national employment-law review.
tasks.human_edge: Recommend a remedy that addresses the underlying practice and can withstand challenge from affected people and decision makers.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on whether approved corrective actions are working.

tasks.altitude: The officer reviews exceptions and evidence rather than assembling each report manually. The role can gain a standing right to request remedial progress reviews; approval of remedies and spending remains with authorised managers.

reach.task: Choose and fund corrective actions across recruitment and progression.
reach.learn: How to connect findings to feasible remedies, accountable owners, and outcome measures.
Pay structures, job comparability, and the practical effects of proposed adjustments.

evidence.claim: Reconciliation, calculations, charts, and template assembly are suitable for deterministic code.
Generated narrative needs factual validation and human assessment of corrective recommendations.
The documented report failure involving invented sources supports traceable citations and factual checks.
A determining score can fall within the GDPR automated-decision analysis, as illustrated by the SCHUFA judgment.

assumptions: Reports are internal management reports; external filings require a separate authorised release step.
The report pipeline reuses approved survey statistics rather than duplicating survey analysis.
Protected-characteristic data are included only where lawful and necessary.
Automated calculations do not make findings of unlawful discrimination or individual employment decisions.
Build ranges describe an initial standalone implementation; shared survey infrastructure can reduce duplicate effort.
Time shares are planning estimates.
EU law applies, alongside applicable national employment and consultation rules.
unknowns: Required report formats, audiences, and reporting periods.
Selection-stage definitions and availability of reliable denominators.
Lawful demographic data coverage and disclosure thresholds.
Who can approve remedies, budgets, publication, and external disclosure.
Existing survey pipeline, action register, and integration access.
Whether new reporting constitutes employee monitoring under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Which report sections can use fixed prose and avoid a model entirely?
What reconciliation rules detect changed selection-stage definitions?
Which outcome measures can distinguish action completion from actual improvement?
How can narrative validation detect unsupported causal claims as well as incorrect numbers?
new_work: Resolve data quality exceptions and changed definitions.
Review narrative, limitations, and source references.
Maintain templates, calculations, and disclosure controls.
Check action status evidence and overdue commitments.
Audit recipient permissions and publication failures.

role.altitude: The week shifts from date chasing, data preparation, and document assembly toward procedural fairness, difficult conversations, and evidence-led remedies. Explicit mandates can add rights to convene urgent reviews and initiate scoped fact-finding; findings, employment actions, and spending retain named human decision makers.
reach: Labor relations specialists: align complaint handling with representation rights and national rules.
Training and development specialists: turn recurring concerns into effective supervisor practice.
Compensation and job analysis specialists: develop defensible comparison groups and pay-related investigations.
Human resources managers: translate findings into funded remedies and evaluate outcomes.
skills_to_grow: Statistical interpretation, uncertainty, confounding, and response bias.
GDPR data minimisation, special-category processing, and disclosure control.
Assessment of applicable EU AI Act and national consultation requirements.
Complaint process design and sensitive facilitation.
Source-grounded drafting review and factual validation.
Data definitions, integration acceptance, and corrective action evaluation.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early-warning and remedy-review service that combines confidential complaint process monitoring, targeted employee listening, and reproducible employment-practice analysis. The officer uses the evidence to initiate focused reviews and help managers choose effective remedies, without automating discrimination findings or employment decisions.
